  1. Description

Annotation Interface JsonRecord

@Documented @Retention(CLASS) @Target(TYPE) public @interface JsonRecord

Marks a record, or a sealed interface of records, that documents bind to, with [JsonParser#parseAs(Class, byte[])], and that JsonWriter.formatAs(Class, Object) writes.

@JsonRecord
record Order(long id, Customer customer, List<Line> lines, @Nullable Instant shipped) {}
record Customer(String name, @JsonName("e-mail") String email) {}
record Line(String product, int quantity, BigDecimal price) {}

Order order = new JsonParser().parseAs(Order.class, body);

The annotation processor of the be.imgn.json:json-processor artifact generates the code that reads and writes the type straight from and to the stream, without reflection, and registers it as a JsonBinder service; on the module path, the module of the type must declare it: provides be.imgn.json.JsonBinder with .... The processor rejects at compile time a type it cannot bind. The records, sealed interfaces and enums the type refers to are bound the same way, without the annotation.

Each component of a record is a member of an object, named as the component, or as its JsonName. A missing member is an error, unless the component is annotated @Nullable (any annotation of that simple name), which makes it null, as does a null member. A member that no component takes is skipped, or rejected with UnknownMembers.REJECT. When written, a null component is omitted, unless the writer writes it.

The types bound, anything else being a compile error:

  • String, from a string;
  • long, int, short, byte and their boxes, from a number whose value is an integer in their range, such as 12, 1.0 or 1e2;
  • double, float and their boxes, from a number, to its nearest value;
  • boolean and Boolean, from a boolean;
  • BigInteger and BigDecimal, from a number, exactly;
  • Instant, OffsetDateTime, LocalDate, LocalTime, LocalDateTime and Duration, from a string in ISO-8601;
  • UUID and URI, from a string in their canonical form;
  • an enum, from a string naming one of its constants, or its JsonName;
  • a record, from an object;
  • a sealed interface of records, from an object naming the record, as JsonTagMember or JsonWrapper lay it out;
  • List<T> and Set<T>, from an array of values that bind to T, a set rejecting duplicates;
  • Map<String, T>, from an object of values that bind to T;
  • JsonValue and its subtypes, as they are: a @Nullable JsonValue component is null for a missing member, and JsonNull.INSTANCE for a null one.

Lists, sets and maps keep the order of the document, and cannot be modified. A record whose constructor throws is an error at the position of its object, with the exception as its cause.
